subject: PO constraints: multi-entity tax withholdings & packaging options
messages:
From: Janet Liu <jliu@carewell.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: procure-ap@carewell.com
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood billing / PO requirements and packaging questions

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement needs a few clarifications before we can issue the PO:

- CareWell is a multi-entity buyer (CareWell US, CareWell Europe). Our ERP requires separate invoicing for each legal entity unless the vendor can provide a consolidated statement with per-entity breakdowns.
- For cross-border services we typically apply a 10% withholding unless we receive an exemption certificate from the vendor.
- Our standard terms are Net45; however, we can discuss milestone billing for implementation items.
- We also need to understand packaging: our engineering team is evaluating seat-based (per-seat) vs usage (token-based) billing. Any suggestions on discounts or prepay options for a 12–24 month commitment?

I've attached our PO template (CareWell_PO_Template.xlsx). Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
1) accept split invoices by entity and/or provide consolidated statements with per-entity line items;
2) handle gross-up for withholding or provide the necessary tax documentation to avoid withholding;
3) offer any packaging/discount flexibility for a 12–24 month preferred term?

If easier, we can schedule a quick call with procurement and tax to align.

Thanks,
Janet Liu
Senior Procurement Manager
CareWell Health

--
Attachment: CareWell_PO_Template.xlsx (Excel - 24KB)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Janet Liu <jliu@carewell.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood billing / PO requirements and packaging questions

Janet — thanks for the clear list and the template. Quick answers inline and a suggested path forward.

1) Invoicing by entity: Redwood can issue invoices from the legal entity that corresponds to the contract (we have US and EU billing entities). We can either:
   - Send split invoices per legal entity (separate invoice numbers for CareWell US and CareWell EU), or
   - Issue a single consolidated monthly statement that contains per-entity line items and accounting codes to satisfy ERP mapping.

2) Withholding tax: our standard approach is to receive payments gross and treat withholding as the customer's responsibility. If CareWell requires Redwood to gross-up (i.e., pay gross then claim back), we can discuss contractual language, but that will affect pricing. Alternatively, if Redwood can provide a tax exemption/certificate (depends on jurisdiction), that may avoid withholding.

3) Packaging & discounts: we commonly offer three flavors:
   - Pay-as-you-go (token-based) at list rates;
   - Committed usage (monthly minimum) with tiered discounts (2–10% depending on term & volume);
   - Prepaid term (12/24 months) with larger discounts (5–18% depending on prepay).

Suggested next steps:
- Vanessa (cc) will propose a concrete pricing table for 12 and 24 month options and a recommended invoicing pattern (split vs consolidated).
- We can pilot monthly split invoices for the first quarter to ensure ERP reconciliation works, then switch to consolidated statements if preferred.

I've attached our billing options summary for reference.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Janet — looping in Vivek from finance to confirm tax and invoicing mechanics. High level from sales:

- For a 12-month committed usage agreement we can offer a 2% on-invoice discount for monthly billing, or 6% for full 12-month prepay.
- For a 24-month commitment, discounts start at 8% (monthly billing) or 15% (prepay).
- To accommodate CareWell's ERP we recommend either:
    a) split invoices (one per legal entity) OR
    b) consolidated invoice + a detailed CSV statement per invoice that maps lines to CareWell entity codes.

On withholdings: Vivek — can Redwood support gross-up clauses or provide an exemption certificate in your experience? If gross-up is required, we should model the price impact.

Mateo — if procurement is comfortable with the pilot (split invoices for Q1), we can include language in the SOW for the pilot and add a permanent reconciliation flow. I've attached a short diff of the SOW edits we'd propose.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Thanks Vanessa / Mateo. A couple of clarifications from procurement/tax:

- CareWell policy: when a withholding applies for cross-border services, we expect the vendor to either provide an exemption certificate or accept a gross-up. We have limited ability to change that at our side. If Redwood requires the withholding to be customer-handled, the finance team will need guidance on whether to claim the credit.
- For our ERP, split invoices are simplest operationally. Consolidated statements are doable but increase matching work and sometimes trigger AP holds.
- We are leaning towards committed usage (monthly minimum) rather than pure seats. The engineering team wants token-based billing with a committed floor and a monthly true-up. Can your committed usage plan support per-month true-up and prorated credits?

Would Redwood consider the following contract items as a condition of signing:
1) Redwood will issue split invoices by entity for the first 3 months (pilot).
2) Redwood will provide either an exemption certificate within 30 days or accept gross-up (if acceptance, please propose language and price impact).
3) Include a monthly true-up provision in the billing addendum; credits to be applied within the following invoice cycle.

If Redwood can confirm these items, procurement can issue a PO referencing the attached template.

Janet Liu
Senior Procurement Manager
CareWell Health

Janet — appreciate the clear asks. Confirming Redwood's position and next steps:

1) Split invoices pilot: agreed. We will issue separate invoices for CareWell US and CareWell EU for the first three months to validate ERP reconciliation. After Q1 we can revisit switching to consolidated statements if that reduces AP friction.

2) Withholding / gross-up: Vivek — Redwood can accept a gross-up clause for this engagement, but it needs to be priced. As an alternative, we can provide a tax residency/exemption letter where applicable. For cross-border services, if CareWell requires gross-up we propose adding a Contract Exhibit that specifies the gross-up calculation and a 3% administrative fee to cover handling/withholding reconciliation.

3) Committed usage + monthly true-up: Redwood supports a monthly committed floor with a per-month true-up and credits applied on the subsequent invoice. We will reflect that in the billing addendum.

Commercial offer:
- 12-month committed usage with monthly true-up: 2% on-invoice discount; or 6% for full prepay.
- If CareWell signs a 24-month commitment we can do 10% on-invoice or 15% prepay.

Operationally: please send the signed PO referencing both legal entities to invoices@redwood.com and cc vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com. We'll return redlined SOW + billing addendum within 48 hours. Can we aim to have the PO in place by Apr 15? If yes, we'll stand up the account and schedule a 30-minute kickoff with engineering to confirm token mapping.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
